Punctuation is declared for a document and again inside one index's own
declaration, and the nearer declaration wins key by key. This document writes
three different glyphs to say so: the document sets both keys, the second index
resets one of them, and so that index prints its own mark between a term and
its cross-references while still printing the document's mark between two
cross-references.

Each index files two cross-references on one term, which is the entry that
prints both marks in one line.

## The first index {#site-first}

A term to point at: [Jadeite]{.index index="minerals"}. The term that points at
it twice: [Nephrite]{.index index="minerals" see="Jadeite"
see-also="Jadeite"}.

## The second index {#site-second}

A term to point at: [Electrum]{.index index="alloys"}. The term that points at
it twice: [Pewter]{.index index="alloys" see="Electrum" see-also="Electrum"}.
